data.title:
Small routines build
durable recall
data.subtitle: A synthetic study of practice windows and delayed retrieval
data.metadata: Teaching demonstration · all people and observations are fictional

data.title: A shared protocol makes evidence comparable
data.basis: Illustrative design: surveys describe context; a trial tests the intervention.

steps.heading: Practice
steps.body:
5 weeks of retrieval
One short daily session

sources.heading: 360 surveys
sources.body: Describe routines and preferred windows; no causal inference.

sources.heading: 24 interviews
sources.body: Explain interruptions and barriers during the study.

sources.heading: 168-person trial
sources.body: Compares a shared protocol with self-directed practice.

data.note: Attrition: 3 in protocol, 4 in comparison; all values are synthetic.

data.title: Delayed recall is higher in the protocol group
data.basis: Synthetic endpoint: recall score at week 12, on a 0–100 scale.
data.dotCaption: Each circle = 10 percentage points; fractional sector is proportional.

notes.heading: Interpretation
notes.body: A 30-point gap is illustrated here. This demonstration does not establish a real treatment effect.

notes.heading: Measurement basis
notes.body: The same task and follow-up window apply to both fictional groups.

data.title: Practice windows show different recall scores
data.basis: Synthetic observational grouping; self-selected timing is not randomized.

notes.heading: Pattern worth testing
notes.body: The early window has a higher score in this fabricated dataset. A future trial would test this signal.

notes.heading: Boundary of the claim
notes.body: Timing may reflect routine and environment. Association alone does not identify the cause.

data.plotNote: Scores share a zero baseline; values and units remain editable.

data.title: A slower decay model explains persistence
data.basis: Illustrative half-life model; curves are derived examples, not observed evidence.

definitions.heading: Model definition
definitions.body: A half-life describes the time needed for retention to halve. The curve uses the same parameter shown in the legend.

definitions.heading: Review cadence
definitions.body: Ticks mark planned reviews. They are annotations, not jumps in this smooth illustrative decay model.

data.plotNote: Modeled curves; review ticks are supplied by content.
data.modelNote: Both series start at one. The model is illustrative; fit and uncertainty are not claimed.

data.title: Benefit and persistence differ across segments
data.basis: Synthetic survey groups; outcomes and timing are fictional self-reports.
data.footnote: Survey sample is separate from the trial; totals are synthetic.
data.takeaway: Tailor delivery to context; the strongest score and adherence need not coincide.

data.title: One fictional routine shows delivery feasibility
data.basis: Single synthetic case; an illustration cannot establish population effects.

notes.heading: Context
notes.body: A fictional learner uses a regular travel window. The image shell indicates where an authorized case photo could sit.

notes.heading: Routine
notes.body: A short practice block and three planned reviews reduce scheduling friction. This is illustrative workflow content.

notes.heading: Process evidence
notes.body: Completed sessions and test scores are tracked separately. Missing observations must stay visible in a real study.

data.resultNote: The direction is consistent with the fictional group example; no inference is implied.
data.caution: Fictional case: descriptive feasibility evidence only.

data.title: Turn the evidence into a reviewable next step
data.basis: Synthetic teaching plan; owners, dates and thresholds are illustrative.

actions.heading: Choose a stable window
actions.why: Why: A regular context reduces scheduling friction.
actions.how: How: Attach the session to an existing routine.

actions.heading: Keep the session bounded
actions.why: Why: A visible endpoint makes completion observable.
actions.how: How: Stop at the agreed limit and log completion.

actions.heading: Review the old material
actions.how: How: Use the planned review ticks, then reassess.

data.reviewLabel: Next review · decide whether to extend the pilot
